To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) object function is an effective feature for scene object recognition and (ii) object function is well described by the way people use the objects.
We show how to learn discriminative object models that predict human poses and appearance from a large number of time-lapse scenes.

(1) object recognition performance can be significantly improved by incorporating human pose information and (2) human poses can be predicted in new scenes by using the object function learned from human observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the question of what objects are used for in everyday life and how they are used.
the following contributions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented method is a significant step forward for recognizing objects by the way how people interact with them, and it is a step towards understanding human-object interactions in a scene.
the proposed method can be used to recognize the object function in a scene, and that the recognition of object function is more accurate when the human pose is taken into account.
the proposed approach is able to recognize objects and predict human poses in realistic scenes with a high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to learn object function models from long-term observation of people and demonstrate that they can improve object recognition.
we learn object models that are more robust to appearance changes and that can predict object function.
we show that human-object interactions are a rich source of information for object recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way we interact with objects is more discriminative than the appearance of objects themselves.
human observations can provide valuable information to improve the recognition of everyday objects and their functions.
human-object interactions are a powerful source of information for object recognition and can be used to predict object function in new situations.
